previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, chronic diarrhea, and malnutrition with G-tube dependence, was admitted for acute nausea, vomiting, and worsening diarrhea over two days. He was found to have Influenza B, likely contributing to his gastrointestinal symptoms. He showed signs of dehydration with dry mucous membranes and received 3 liters of IV fluids. Workup included negative stool studies for C. difficile, norovirus, salmonella, shigella, and campylobacter, and no evidence of CMV reactivation. Liver ultrasound showed stable findings with patent vasculature and mild biliary dilation unchanged from prior. His immunosuppressive and pain medications were continued, while antidiarrheals were held initially and restarted when infection was ruled out. He gradually tolerated oral intake, and his symptoms improved. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete a 10-day course of oseltamivir, resume G-tube feeds, and follow up with his transplant and primary care teams.
problems: Influenza due to other identified influenza virus with other respiratory manifestations
